units.why: Still blocked on plate solving. sim_sky.rs has landed and is compiled into the shipped bridge (lib/libskotiq_bridge.so, 16:54 today), and its own ignored test passes ('downloaded frame solved, centre error 0.5"' from cargo test -p skotiq_bridge --lib sim_sky_wiring -- --ignored). But in the running desktop app it does not engage: with sim camera + sim mount connected, the plate solver configured at ~/.local/share/skotiq-audit/astap/bin (astap_cli + full D05), and the mount slewed to RA 05h30m / Dec +22, the app's own solve logged 'Running ASTAP: .../astap_cli -f .../0002.fits -z 2 -d .../astap/bin -wcs' then 'ASTAP exited with non-zero status 1'. Independent hinted solves of the captured frames at both plausible plate scales (0.582 deg for 400 mm, 0.2327 deg for the 1000 mm default) and a full blind all-sky solve all returned 'No solution found'. No 'sim sky: indexed ... area files' line ever appears in the app log, i.e. sim_sky_view returns None in the shipped binary. Without a WCS the Slew & Center / dashboard / planetarium entry points cannot produce the dialog.

Same root cause as centering_dialog: details_panel is part of catalog_overlay_widget, which live_preview_area only builds once the preview holds a plate-solved frame with a WCS. The simulated camera does not render the catalogue sky in the shipped app (see the centering_dialog evidence), so no simulated frame can be solved and the overlay never mounts.

findings.title: The "database recovered" notice never appears in the one case where the data is recoverable
findings.detail: Reproduced live in a scratch profile, three controlled variants, same marker payload each time. (a) Real corruption — first 4096 bytes of skotiq.db overwritten, pre-flight rotated it to skotiq-corrupt-1786311314614-skotiq.db: dialog SHOWN, 'Re-checked just now: SQLite still cannot read this file', OK button (screenshot /tmp/ns-forced/db1f.png). (b) Marker staged with NO skotiq-corrupt-* file present: dialog SHOWN, marker left on disk until acknowledged. (c) Marker staged with a HEALTHY skotiq-corrupt-*.db beside it (a byte copy of the live database), run TWICE: NO dialog at any point across ~30 s of polling the accessibility tree, and the .recovered-on-*.txt marker was deleted within 4 s of launch — the launcher only acknowledges after the dialog reports shown, so the dialog was pushed and then vanished without user action. Variant (c) is exactly the case the code exists for: the file comments describe builds that quarantined healthy databases after a transient open failure, and it is the only branch that renders the 'Restore my database' button. As shipped, a user whose good database was quarantined is told nothing, the one-shot notice is burned, and the restore affordance never appears. I reproduced the symptom but did not isolate the mechanism, so I did not attempt a fix — guessing here would relocate the defect rather than close it.

findings.title: S9 is not closed in the shipped app: the simulated camera still does not render the catalogue sky, so nothing can be plate-solved
findings.detail: The plan lists centering_dialog and details_panel as unblocked because sim_sky.rs landed. It has landed and is compiled into the shipped bridge (bundle lib/libskotiq_bridge.so and native/.../target/release/libskotiq_bridge.so are the same md5, built after the source), and its own end-to-end test passes: cargo test -p skotiq_bridge --lib sim_sky_wiring -- --ignored printed 'downloaded frame solved, centre error 0.5"'. In the running desktop app it never engages. Setup: sim camera + sim mount connected from a saved profile (400 mm / 3.76 um -> the app itself computed 1.94 arcsec/px), plate solver preference loaded at startup as astap=".../skotiq-audit/astap/bin/astap_cli" catalog=".../skotiq-audit/astap/bin" (full D05), mount unparked and slewed to RA 05h30m / Dec +22 (the slew was accepted and the RA readout changed, which also proves get_sim_mount().status.connected is true, since sim_gate refuses a slew on a disconnected mount). The app's own auto-solve logged 'Running ASTAP: .../astap_cli -f .../0002.fits -z 2 -d .../astap/bin -wcs' then 'ASTAP exited with non-zero status 1'. Independent hinted solves of the captured frames at 0.582 deg (400 mm) and 0.2327 deg (the 1000 mm SIM default) and a full 180-degree blind solve all returned 'No solution found'. Two consecutive 2 s Light frames at a fixed pointing share ZERO of their 40 brightest median-filtered sources, i.e. the field is re-randomised every exposure rather than being a static sky. No 'sim sky: indexed N area files' line is ever emitted, so sim_sky_view is returning None in the shipped binary while returning a field under cargo test. Consequence: every plate-solve-dependent surface remains unexercisable offline (Slew & Center, centering_dialog, framing wizard, mosaic tile solving, meridian-flip recentre, blind solve, catalog overlay + details_panel, polar alignment's solve path).

findings.title: Catalog Setup advertised the Complete package's contents no matter which package was selected
findings.detail: Reproduced live: with both catalogs missing the startup dialog rendered 'HYG Star Database ~120,000 stars' and 'OpenNGC ~13,000 DSOs (NGC/IC)' under green ticks, above a selector defaulting to Standard (~30 MB). Selecting Essential (~10 MB) left both lines unchanged (screenshots /tmp/ns-forced/cat1c.png and cat2c.png). Those are the Complete figures; the enum documents Essential as ~9,000 stars / ~2,000 objects and Standard as ~40,000 / ~8,000, so the default choice was advertised as three times, and the smallest as thirteen times, what it installs. The package rows themselves only offered a megabyte figure and a vague blurb, which is not what an imager needs to choose.
findings.fixSummary: CatalogPackage now carries approximateStarCount/approximateDsoCount as fields (they existed only in doc comments) plus a formatCatalogCount helper; the dialog's two summary lines read the SELECTED package, and every package row now states '~N stars . ~N DSOs' alongside its size. New test 'the advertised catalog contents follow the selected package' in packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/catalog_setup_dialog_test.dart; reverting the header change makes it fail with 'Found 0 widgets with text "~40,000 stars"'.

findings.title: Native settings, equipment profiles and the plate-solver preference live in ~/Documents, outside every isolation knob
findings.detail: Found by accident and then confirmed twice. A brand-new scratch profile (fresh SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR, fresh XDG_DATA_HOME) opened Settings > Plate Solving already populated with '/tmp/ns-audit/fake-astap/astap' — a path left behind by a different sweep on 2026-08-01, and a path that does not exist. The store is ~/Documents/Skotiq/profiles/{profiles,settings,platesolver}.json: getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() joined with 'Skotiq/profiles', which honours neither SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR nor XDG_DATA_HOME. It is also genuinely shared at runtime: after I pointed platesolver.json at a real ASTAP install, a concurrently-running sweep overwrote it mid-session with /opt/HOSTMARKER paths, which silently disarmed the simulated sky for my next exposure. Two problems for a user, not just for sweeps: application configuration is written into the Documents folder (cloud-synced on most desktops, and where profile export/import already goes), and the documented isolation env var only isolates half the state. I redirected my own runs by pointing XDG_CONFIG_HOME at a user-dirs.dirs that moves XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR, which works but is not something the harness does today.

findings.title: The database-recovery dialog has no maximum width and runs the full window
findings.detail: On the 1600x1000 harness window the recovered-database AlertDialog spans essentially edge to edge (screenshot /tmp/ns-forced/db1f.png): body lines run ~150 characters, far past a readable measure, and it does not match the rest of the app, which constrains dialogs through AdaptiveDialogConstraints. This is the first thing a user sees after losing their data, so it is worth looking deliberate.

findings.title: A transient alert card never says whether the target is up
findings.detail: Live on the Observing Alerts tab with two seeded First Light detections: the card shows type, classification, delta-mag, state badge, RA/Dec, and on expand Source / Discovered / Last Updated / Notes. Nowhere does it show altitude now, or a rise/set or transit time. For an alert-driven 'go look now' surface that is the first question — the whole point of the Queue button is deciding whether tonight is the night — and the app already computes altitude-now for planner candidates (the planner exposes an 'Alt now' filter). Today the user has to press Framing or Queue to find out the object is below the horizon.

findings.title: Harness limitation: drive_linux.py cannot type any value beginning with '-'
findings.detail: Not an app defect, but it silently narrows what every sweep can test. `type` shells out to `xdotool type --clearmodifiers --delay 30 <text>`; xdotool parses a leading '-' as an option, so typing '-105.0' into the onboarding longitude field crashed with CalledProcessError and the field stayed empty. Every negative latitude, longitude, declination and temperature offset in the app is therefore untypeable by the harness — I had to switch my scratch site to the eastern hemisphere. `--` before the text, or xdotool's --file -, fixes it.
